rules.rule: Diagnose probable heart failure with BP ≥ 180/110 (hypertension diagnosis)
rules.problem: 'heart failure likely' → probable is right. Conditioning on BP ≥ 180/110 is a reading of the box layout; the page does not literally say heart failure is only likely at that BP, so the BP conjunct could be seen as an added restriction (defensible for a page-scoped rule).

Level Urgent matches the box heading 'Give urgent attention'. The structure and(BP ≥ 180/110, or(all box items)) is faithful to the header, but it applies the emergency-column items (chest pain, dyspnoea, severe HF, kidney failure) at the DBP ≥ 110 threshold where the page specifies DBP ≥ 130; this over-triggers only in the narrow band DBP 110-129 with SBP < 180, which the header arguably covers anyway. The house pattern of referencing (active_condition X) for the box's likely diagnoses was not used; functionally equivalent. The page also distinguishes 'refer urgently' (emergency) from 'refer same day' (urgency), which a single Urgent level flattens; the brief says not to escalate without explicit page wording, so this is noted, not a defect.

Nothing invented, but the page's lower flowchart is not encoded at all: 'Diagnose mild hypertension' (BP 140/90-159/99 on repeat), 'Diagnose moderate hypertension' (160/100-179/109 on repeat) and 'Diagnose severe hypertension' (BP confirmed ≥ 180/110) are explicit diagnoses the page makes, and 'If < 30 years, refer to exclude secondary cause' and 'If > 65 years and no co-morbid disease, start treatment only when BP > 160/90' are age-gated logic. The repeat-reading requirement may not be expressible, but at least the severe hypertension diagnosis (confirmed ≥ 180/110, no urgent symptoms) and the mild/moderate bands deserve rules or an explicit remaining-questions entry.

summary: No claim is unsupported or wrong: every condition in the six rules traces to the red box, with the right thresholds (180/110 vs 180/130), the right qualifiers and the right certainty (every 'likely' is probable). The most consequential gap is coverage, not invention: the page's explicit mild/moderate/severe hypertension diagnoses and the age-gated advice below the box are not encoded. Within the box, 'Muscle weakness' is broader than 'weakness on 1 or both sides' (Muscle weakness of limb is closer), and the two kidney items lose their eGFR thresholds (CKD stage 5 / Renal impairment are proxies), which should be recorded as known approximations.
